title: Gordo
desc: Affection that arrives sounding like an insult
setting: Lucía has called you gordo twice this week and Roberto has explained why you must not be offended.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.en: What are you up to, gordo?

options.feedback: Answer in the same currency. Gordo, negra, flaco: they all sound like insults and none of them are, and using one back says you have understood.
Perfectly normal. She used the affectionate word and you did not, which she will notice without saying so.
That is the nicest thing she has said to you all week. Refusing it tells her the door is closed.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Ay, mirá vos. ¿Y quién te enseñó eso?
steps.en: Well, look at you. And who taught you that?

options.es: Roberto, que se rió de mí media hora.
options.en: Roberto, who laughed at me for half an hour.
options.feedback: Telling her you had to be taught is funnier and warmer than pretending you knew. Nobody expects a chele to arrive knowing this.
True and a little pleased with itself. The story of how you learned it is the better answer.
You went silent for two hours the first time she said it. She will find that out eventually and it will be better if she hears it from you.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: La primera vez no me contestaste en dos horas, gordo.
steps.en: The first time you did not answer me for two hours, gordo.

options.es: Es que en mi país eso se toma feo. Ya aprendí.
options.en: It is that where I am from that is taken badly. I have learned now.
options.feedback: Name the difference once, say you have got it, and let it go. Here affection is said backwards on purpose, and that is precisely what makes it affection.
Fine. She was teasing rather than complaining, and an explanation would have been better than an apology.

options.es: Es que fue un poco fuerte.
options.en: It was a bit strong, though.
options.feedback: You are still arguing that she was rude. She was not, and you have already been told so by two different people.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Vení a la casa el domingo. Mi mamá quiere conocerte bien.
steps.en: Come to the house on Sunday. My mother wants to get to know you properly.

options.en: I will be there. What shall I bring?
options.feedback: You said yes and asked the only question that matters. Arriving at doña Elena's house with your hands empty is not a mistake you get to make twice.
You are going, which is the main thing. What you carry through that door is half of what she is judging.

options.en: And do I have to go?
options.feedback: It was not really an invitation. Her mother wanting to see you is the next step and there is no version where you decline it.
